\captionof{figure}{Grouped comparison of ROC-AUC and PR-AUC for the frozen classical head and the three frozen quantum neural-network (QNN) heads at the 22,099-event benchmark. All QNN values were obtained with PennyLane's \texttt{default.qubit} statevector simulator on CPU using the same frozen $z \in \mathbb{R}^{16}$ representation as the classical head. These simulated results are not measurements from quantum hardware and do not establish quantum advantage.}
\label{fig:benchmark-22k-auc}

\captionof{figure}{ROC-AUC of the frozen classical head and frozen QNN heads as the benchmark size increases from 1,200 to 5,599 and 22,099 events. The 1,200-event benchmark contains only the classical head and QNN $L=2$ results; QNN $L=4$ and $L=6$ are left unavailable rather than interpolated or inferred. QNN curves denote classically simulated CPU results.}
\label{fig:benchmark-scaling-roc}

\captionof{figure}{Accuracy comparison for the frozen classical head and classically simulated frozen QNN heads at 22,099 events. The comparison uses the same test split and frozen latent representation for all heads; it is a descriptive benchmark and does not imply quantum computational advantage.}
\label{fig:benchmark-22k-accuracy}
